endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: Establish a change management plan among developer and implementer teams, e.g. determine which party will be responsible for performance monitoring, updates of model and interface, etc.

endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Specify which party is responsible for pursuing, maintaining, or reporting changes to FDA authorization.

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Device Software Functions: Lifecycle Management and Marketing Submission Recommendations (draft guidance)
Diverging regulatory DNA in adaptive medical AI: US agility and EU accountability in lifecycle governance
endorsements.quote: Operationally, developers must maintain update documentation and performance monitoring plans, healthcare institutions must enable data capture and incident reporting in routine workflows, and regulators/notified bodies must define acceptance criteria and escalation pathways that translate post-market signals into governance actions.

commentary.bottom_line: No study supplied for this recommendation tests whether a documented change management process that assigns developer, vendor, and implementer responsibilities reduces risk from code, data, environment, or model changes. The recommendation rests on four endorsements, including FDA draft guidance and two CHAI frameworks, rather than on measured outcomes.

perspectives.view: The evidence base contains zero studies that test the practice and zero studies that document the hazard. Certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence. The four endorsements reflect expert and regulatory consensus, and consensus of this kind does not substitute for comparative data on whether assigned change responsibilities reduce undetected performance shifts after updates.

FDA draft lifecycle guidance lists change management strategies among its recommendations, and one CHAI playbook asks parties to specify who reports changes to FDA authorization. A commentary on US and EU approaches assigns update documentation to developers and incident reporting to institutions. These sources describe expected roles, and none reports outcomes from applying them.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that compare sites with and without documented, role-assigned change management plans and measure outcomes such as time to detect post-update performance degradation, the share of updates that receive revalidation, version-tracking errors, and patient-level harm events. No study, including any study of the underlying hazard, was supplied to establish how often unclear update accountability leads to harm.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no test included Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. It remains unknown whether change management processes perform differently in safety-net settings, where bargaining power with vendors and informatics staffing may be more limited and where post-update performance shifts could affect these populations without being detected.
